page.layout: Running head at top, page number 152 at left. Above the text, two coin medallions side by side (woodcut illustrations, left P. Clodius, right Fulvia). Below them one block of running text in two paragraphs, full width, no notes in the margins.

main_text.l: P. CLODIVS vir claris parentibus ortus,iuuenis quidē
audax,incestuosus ac seditiosus,cūm amore Pompeiæ Cæsaris
coniugis flagraret,clam eius domū ingreditur,vestem ac habi-
tum psaltriæ indutus:spéq; latēdi mulieres abductus ob adole-
scentiæ formam,genāsque nondū pubentes turbæ earum,quæ
tum in ædeCasaris sacrum inacessum viris agebant,immistus,
ad Pompeiam ingreditur:deprehensus ac agnitus,etiā Cicero-
ne teste,accusatur:verūm iudices tū metu,tum largitione,tum
fauore eum absoluunt. fit deinde Tribunus plebis, & factione
sua Ciceronē in exilium agit, anno à mundo cōdito 3906. ante
Christum seruatorē natum 56.cuius domum ac villas incendit:
reliqua bona hastæ subiicit:attamē emit nemo. Tandem à Mi-
lone Clodius occiditur, accusatur Milo, patronúmque habet
Ciceronē, iam antè ab exilio reuocatum. Vide Plutar.in Cice.
& Cæs.item Appi.de ciui.Ro.bel.li.2.
FVLVIA, uxor P. Clodij, quæ postea M. antonio nupsit,
non muliebres artes, non familiam regere curabat,nec priua-
tum hominem superare contendebat, sed magistratus gerere,
& imperatibus imperare,vt sibi magnas gratias deberet Cleo-
patra, quod institutum ab ea Antonium acceperit. hæc clam
noctu profecta, Ciceroni Catilinæ detexit insidias, eúmque
cōmonefecit vt Cethegum,eiusque comites præcaueret. Plut.
in Cice. & Anto.

page.notes: Coin legends are printed in the two medallions and are not transcribed as running text: left medallion around the head "CLODIVS" with "P." and "AED"-type marks at the lower edge [?]; right medallion around the head "FVLVIA" [?]. Words in the paragraphs marked with a tilde or acute over a vowel are copied with the mark as printed; some of these marks are uncertain at the scan's resolution. Printed "M .antonio" is copied with its spacing and lower-case initial as printed.
